children: shares rose Monday after Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated an Overweight rating and a $122 price target, implying roughly 89% upside from current levels. Analyst Andres Sheppard called the stock a good entry point ahead of two potentially transformative catalysts: Neutron's first launch and the expected closing of Rocket Lab's acquisition of Iridium.

Rocket Lab provides launch services, spacecraft components and satellite systems to commercial and government customers. Its Electron rocket serves the small-launch market, while HASTE supports hypersonic testing and Neutron is being developed as a substantially larger medium-lift vehicle.
Neutron is central to Cantor's bullish case.

Rocket Lab is still targeting its first launch later this year. The rocket is designed to carry roughly 13,000 kilograms of payload, compared with about 300 kilograms for Electron, dramatically expanding the missions Rocket Lab can pursue.

Management expects Neutron launches to generate roughly $50 million to $55 million each and is targeting as many as 20 flights per engine. Sheppard sees the rocket eventually emerging as an alternative to SpaceX's Falcon 9.

Rocket Lab's existing execution gives Cantor additional confidence. The company completed its 96th Electron mission on September 19, marking its 17th launch of 2026, and has another 15 dedicated missions planned for Synspective through the end of the decade.

Rocket Lab has raised $1.944 billion through an at-the-market share offering, removing a major financing hurdle for the transaction. The deal is expected to close in mid-2027, subject to regulatory approval, and Sheppard expects the combined company to roughly double annual revenue.

Rocket Lab's valuation now depends increasingly on execution rather than its existing Electron business alone. Investors should watch whether Neutron launches on schedule, reaches commercial reliability and begins converting its much larger payload capability into $50 million-plus missions. The Iridium transaction brings another layer of upside but also integration and dilution risk after Rocket Lab issued roughly 29.3 million shares. Successful Neutron milestones combined with regulatory approval for Iridium would materially strengthen Cantor's $122 bull case; delays in either could quickly compress expectations.

title: Cantor Sees Whopping Upside Ahead for Rocket Lab Stock
